source.title: Packet analyzer
source.source_scope: Capabilities, uses, capture architecture, wired/wireless visibility, capture modes, storage, decoding, traffic generation/testing, hardware analyzers, operational/security uses, lawful interception, notable tools, references and related concepts.

design_principles: Packet analyzer is a first-class operational tool node.
Capture, decode, analyze, store, display, generate, and test are modeled as distinct capabilities/processes.
Capture visibility is modeled as a function of network topology, capture location, interfaces, and modes.
Full-packet and header-only capture are separate modes with explicit storage/privacy tradeoffs.
Wired and wireless capture architectures are distinct branches.
Security, operations, debugging, compliance, and testing uses are represented as downstream applications.
Notable analyzers are retained as individual nodes rather than collapsed into a generic list.
Source-derived legal and privacy framing is preserved without adding external legal claims.

nodes.label: Definition and operation
nodes.description: Packet analyzers can be software or hardware and analyze/log network traffic; packet capture intercepts and logs traffic; packets may be decoded and analyzed against specifications.

nodes.label: Terminology
nodes.description: Wireless analyzers and Wi-Fi analyzers are packet analyzers for wireless traffic; protocol analyzer can be broader, though terms are often interchangeable.
